events.name: The Final Choice
events.intro: Dawn. The eleventh floor: a corridor of grey carpet, and at the end of it a door with a brass plate, PRESIDENT. Otis is behind you with his sleeves rolled; Faye has a ledger under her arm that isn't the one she usually carries. In your hand is a key card: ELEVENTH FLOOR. ALL DOORS. Behind the brass plate, unhurried: Giovanni: "It's open. It's been open for an hour. I was curious whether you'd knock." On the fire stairs, one flight down, a man in a brown coat has stopped tying his shoe. Looker: "I am not here. I am a man with a shoe." Faye holds out the other ledger. Faye: "Four thousand, one hundred and twelve. Names and addresses. I copied it out by hand; it took a year of lunches. I don't know who to give it to. I've decided that's your job." You hold two things now: a key and a list. The Final Choice is who gets which.

success.text: You open the door. He's at the desk, and he nods to you as if you'd brought the post. The list goes back into Faye's bag.

You close the brass-plated door, from the outside, and turn the key. A pause, from inside. Giovanni: "Ah. You're one of the looking kind after all. Matori did say "doesn't know yet."" A chair creaks. Giovanni: "I'll wait. It's a good door. I chose it." Otis: "What do we do?" Faye: "We go down. Floor by floor. And I read the book out at each one."

You throw the key card down the stairwell. A hand comes out of a brown coat and catches it. Looker: "I asked for evidence. You have brought me a building." He's already on a radio. "All units. Eleventh floor. We have the door, the list, and a person in a uniform who is, I am told, looking."

choices.label: "It's a good plan. It doesn't need you."

success.text: You open the door, go in, and shut it behind you. He doesn't turn round from the window. Giovanni: "...No. It doesn't. That's how I knew it was good." Now he turns. Giovanni: "I've been waiting eleven years for somebody downstairs to say that. I'd rather hoped it would be my son."

remembers.notice: Matori is at the lift as you pass, tablet under her arm. "Did you find it?" she asks, and doesn't wait for the answer.
Matori: "You sat with me on a bench. I've moved his one o'clock. I'd have moved it anyway. I'd like you to think I moved it for that."

events.name: Phase 1: Hold the Line
events.intro: The Saffron police and Gym trainers with warrants contest the lobby, the labs and the stairs. You place the squad.

choices.label: Otis in the lobby, Faye in the labs, you on the stairs.

success.text: In the lobby Otis doesn't fight well; he talks. "Mind the plant, that's the President's." Two officers stop to mind the plant. In the labs, Faye has locked the specimen cabinets and lost the key in her cardigan. The stairs are yours.

choices.label: Keep the squad with you on the stairs.

success.text: The three of you hold the stairs, and the lobby and the labs come up to meet you.

events.name: Phase 2: The Gate Locks
events.intro: The last lock is in your hands. Seat it, and the building is sealed.

success.text: Over the PA: Giovanni: "Building sealed. Please remain where you are. ...House Card: the eighth-floor pantry has a secretary in it who's been here nineteen years. Leave her. She makes the tea."

events.name: Phase 3: The Rival
events.intro: Your rival comes through the freight lift, and stops dead. "You're in it. You're wearing it. Tell me there's a reason. I'll believe nearly anything."

success.text: "Then show me."
"Not without you."

choices.label: "Sixth floor. The Rig Room. There's a switch under the housing, on the left."

success.text: No battle. Your rival looks at you for one long second, and goes. Somewhere below, every Rig in the building goes quiet. Giovanni never learns who.

events.name: Phase 4: The Defender
events.intro: The city's Gym Leader leads the police up the last stair. Sabrina: "This city isn't yours. Give it back."

success.text: She doesn't raise her voice.

events.name: Phase 5: The Roof
events.intro: Rain. The armour, kneeling, cabled. Ein, under an umbrella, writing. Police helicopters are coming in over Saffron. M2, a voice with no mouth: "You. You're on the wrong side of the glass. I can tell. You keep looking at the cables." Giovanni: "Hold ten turns. Then it's done, and nobody need ever switch it on."

success.text: Ten turns. You hold. At the tenth: Giovanni: "There. Orderly. You see? Nobody shouting." The Master Ball's on a cushion. He doesn't pick it up. He looks at it the way he looked at the photograph.

choices.label: Do nothing, and let them see you do it.

success.text: You stand in the rain with your hands at your sides. The game doesn't punish it. M2 notices. M2: "...Ah. One of you has a conscience and a uniform. I've met the uniform. I'd like to meet the other." The tenth turn comes anyway. Giovanni: "There. Orderly."

success.text: He calls his collection to the glass.

choices.label: Show him the boy's drawing of it.

success.text: He looks at it for a long time. Then he signs. The receipt comes back with a second drawing on it, by Mr. Quarrington, of a man in a room full of glass.

choices.label: Leave the receipt, and the money, and wait.

success.text: You leave them on his table and wait in the street. At dusk the door opens, and the Growlithe comes out, and runs for Celadon.

events.name: Audit 2: Forty Crates
events.intro: Entries 2,001 to 2,040: forty crates on the Vermilion freighter, before it sails. The crane operator: "I can put a crate anywhere on that dock. I've never once been asked to put one back." No stealth. Team Ledger walks up the gangway with a clipboard.

success.text: The deck is wet and the crates are stacked high.

events.name: The Deck
events.intro: Major Surge is at the top of the gangway. Major Surge: "What's this? A raid?" Faye: "An inventory check. Head office. You'll have had the memo." There's no memo. She's so sure of herself that he looks for it.

success.text: He finds no memo, and squares up.

failure.text: He looks, and looks, and decides he must have lost it.

events.name: The Hold
events.intro: Major Surge: "No memo, no crates. I don't care whose head office."

success.text: The deck hums with his Pokémon's charge.

events.name: The Crane
events.intro: Forty crates are craned ashore while Surge argues with a telephone.

success.text: The receipt runs to forty lines. The last: "Received by: the dock, and whoever comes to collect. Signed: the crane."

events.name: Audit 3: One Pidgey
events.intro: LEDGER: ENTRY 1. ONE PIDGEY. OWNER: MADAME. STATUS: KEPT. QUERY: IS THIS ENTRY OPEN? Faye: "Forty years. The boy who couldn't pay his tenth. She meant to give it back." It's you who rings her, from the Game Corner's basement. Madame Boss: "Who's this on my line? ...The auditors. Oh, how lovely. I wondered who'd get to entry one. He never looked that far back. It died, dear, eleven years ago. Old age. It's under the plum tree. But the boy's alive. He's seventy. He keeps a ferry at Fuchsia. He never came for it because he was ashamed; I never sent it because I'd got fond. Go and tell him it had a good life. That's the only way that one closes."

success.text: An old man is mending a rope. "A Pidgey? ...I was nine. I traded a marble for it and I couldn't pay the lady's tenth. I've thought about that bird for sixty years. I thought she'd sold it." Faye: "She kept it. Thirty years. It slept on her desk. Here's your receipt." He reads it for a long time. "Returned: the knowledge of one Pidgey. Owner: you, all along. Balance: nil." ENTRY 1: COMPLETED. LEDGER's black tag falls off.

events.name: The Read-Out
events.intro: The night of Silph. Saffron's sealed. Team Ledger walks in through the front. In the lobby there are forty Grunts, and nobody has told them what to do about six people and a tea towel. Faye goes to the reception desk and picks up the building's own PA. Faye: "Good evening. This is an audit. I'll be reading out what each of you is owed. Please remain where you are."

success.text: She starts at the basement.

events.name: The Read-Out
events.intro: Floor by floor, over the speakers, in a level voice. "Basement. Otis Blackthorn: one set of teeth, paid in full. Remy, upper nineteen: eleven weeks' wages, unpaid; and an apology, unpaid." "Fourth floor. Kennel handlers: you were told to stop naming them. Biscuit Two's name is in the book. So's Biscuit One's." "Sixth floor. Dr. Sotheby: one patent, owed." "Ninth. Butch. It's spelled B, U, T, C, H. It's been wrong on your pay slip for nine years. It's right in mine." "Eleventh. Giovanni. One Gym, honestly held, eleven inspections. It's the only entry against your name that's in black." For every person you've helped in Kanto, one Grunt goes home. The building is half empty before anybody throws a Ball. Only Domino stays in the lobby, alone, because she's the only one who isn't owed anything.

success.text: She doesn't make a speech.

events.name: The Eleventh Floor
events.intro: Domino: "Put me in your book, then. Under what?" Faye: ""Expensive."" Domino: "...Accurate." On the eleventh floor, Giovanni is waiting. Giovanni: "I heard it. Every floor. You read my Gym out. In black. Nobody's ever audited me and found something to my credit." He puts the Master Ball on the desk, and LEDGER's original beside it. Giovanni: "Finish the book. I never could. I kept getting to the Pidgey."

success.text: No Boss battle. He goes. The roof is unbolted by six people and a Porygon. Rocket isn't beaten. It's closed, like an account. The Game Corner becomes a bank, of sorts: it lends at a tenth, and gives it back when they can pay. Faye has stopped wearing the uniform under the cardigan. Otis carries, and only good things now. The book is Faye's. Remy gets eleven weeks' back pay and the apology. Matori reads her own entry and laughs, once. Domino is entered as "Expensive." Butch's name is right in the book. Cassidy's balance is nil. The trio are owed nine years and receive it with interest; James cries. Miss Vickery keeps the flag.
